title: Fiber bound for the Razborov encoding
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, and suppose no variable occurs twice within any single term of $f$ (any two literals of a term sharing a variable are equal). Fix natural numbers $s$ and $d$ with $d \le s$, and fix a target restriction $\gamma$. Consider the restrictions $\rho$ that are *bad* — having exactly $s$ free variables while the Boolean function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ computed by $f$ under $\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$ — and that the Razborov encoding sends to $\gamma$, i.e.\ the first component of the encoding of $f$ and $\rho$ with parameters $w, d$ equals $\gamma$. The number of such restrictions $\rho$ is at most $(4w)^d$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
no variable repeats within a term (literals of a term with equal variable are equal)
ρ has exactly s free variables (IsRestriction s ρ)
ρ is bad: dtDepth of the restricted DNF function exceeds d
the Razborov encoding of ρ has first component equal to γ
replaced:
The number of bad $s$-restrictions $\rho$ mapping to a fixed $\gamma$ under the
encoder is at most $(4w)^d$, since each of the $d$ path steps carries
$w \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 4w$ possibilities.
